projects.title: Easy Prep AI
projects.description:
Easy Prep AI is a full-stack mobile application that revolutionizes meal planning by generating recipes based on the food items already in your pantry and fridge.

The application leverages the power of OpenAI’s DALL-E 2 API to generate images from text prompts. In the context of Easy Prep AI, this feature is used to visualize potential meals based on the user’s available ingredients.

For recipe generation, we utilized the Spoonacular API, a comprehensive food recipe API that can search different recipes, nutrients, ingredients, etc. This ensures that the meals suggested by Easy Prep AI are not only possible with the given ingredients but also edible and nutritious.

To provide a wide range of food options and detailed nutritional information, we integrated the Open Food Facts API. As the world’s most extensive open food API, it provides access to a comprehensive database of grocery store foods worldwide. This allows Easy Prep AI to recognize almost any food item and provide detailed nutritional information, such as calorie count, upon request by the user.

The application will be built using Java and React, demonstrating a robust application of AI/ML technologies in a user-friendly mobile application.

This project showcases my ability to integrate multiple APIs and utilize AI/ML technologies to create a practical and innovative solution to everyday challenges.

projects.title: Purple Solor
projects.description:
Purple Solor is a dynamic 3D scene I created to showcase my proficiency in Three.js, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The scene is a testament to the power of Three.js, a cross-browser JavaScript library/API used to create and display animated 3D computer graphics in a web browser.

The scene features ten distinct objects, ranging from geometric shapes like cubes and spheres to a flat plane, all rendered in a vibrant purple hue. Each object is meticulously crafted and positioned, demonstrating my understanding of 3D object modeling.

One of the highlights of Purple Solor is its lighting. The scene utilizes point light, which simulates light radiating from a single point in all directions. This creates a realistic lighting effect, as it allows for the creation of shadows and helps highlight the 3D nature of the objects.

In addition to point light, the scene also features ambient light. Unlike point light, ambient light illuminates all objects in the scene equally, regardless of their position or orientation. This type of light doesn’t cast shadows but contributes to the overall brightness of the scene, ensuring that no part of the scene is entirely in shadow.

Through Purple Solor, I’ve demonstrated my ability to create engaging, interactive 3D scenes using Three.js and standard web technologies. This project underscores my skills in 3D modeling, lighting, and animation, as well as my creativity and attention to detail. It stands as a testament to my capabilities as a web developer and a 3D artist.
